To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the clinical profile, somatization, and brain characteristics of late life depression were similar in patients with early onset depression (EOD) and late onset depression (LOD), 2) response to ECT was significantly higher in LOD, and 3) response to ETC was associated with late onset depression and psychotic symptoms, but not with structural MRI abnormalities.
the clinical profile, somatics and brain characteristics in late life depression (55 years and older) were similar between early and late onset depression.
late life depression patients with an early onset have lower response rates to electroconvulsive treatment (ECT) than late life depression patients that have a late age at onset.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an innovative treatment approach for patients with late-life depression.
the development of an effective, non-invasive and safe treatment for LLD.
the clinical and brain characteristics of late life depression and the response to electroconvulsivetherapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ECT is a highly effective treatment for depression in the elderly, even when vascular burdened.
the response to ECT in LLD is high and that EOD and LOD do not differ in clinical, somatic, or MRI characteristics.
ECT is a very effective treatment in LLD, and that ECT should be the treatment of first choice in patients with LLD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ECT is an effective and safe treatment for LLD, even if patients have somatic comororbidity.

the response to ECT in LLD is associated with a shorter duration of the index episode, the presence of psychotic features, and a late age at onset, and that the presence of brain changes on MRI is not related to the treatment response.
ECT is effective in both EOD and LOD and the response to ECT is superior in LOD.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ECT is an effective treatment for late life depression, and the age at onset does not seem to affect the response rate.
patients with LOD have a better response to ECT than those with EOD.
ECT should be considered as first line treatment in LLD, regardless of the presence of vascular risk factors.
